claims.text: The initial Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni eutectic alloy has a dual-phase lamellar microstructure with an inter-lamellar spacing of about 2 μm.
The initial alloy exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility during room-temperature uniaxial tension.
The proposed treatment uses more than 75% cold-rolling reduction followed by annealing at 900 °C for 5 minutes.
Cold rolling followed by short annealing will convert the coarse lamellae into a patterned nanolamellar structure with spacing below 100 nm.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will not alter the bulk alloy composition.
The targeted inter-lamellar spacing is approximately 40 nm, as observed in similar refractory HEAs.
The treated microstructure will contain coherent interfaces between soft FCC and hard B2 phases.
Severe plastic deformation introduces a high dislocation density and refines the lamellar spacing.
The subsequent anneal stabilizes the refined structure and promotes coherent interfaces.
The patterned configuration permits dislocation shearing of lamellae and dislocation pinning by hard phases, analogous to δ lamellae and γ″ particles in another HEA.
Dislocation transmission and pinning at refined interfaces will reduce interfacial stress concentrations and thereby increase strain hardening and ductility.
The treatment will produce an ultimate tensile strength above 1.4 GPa.
The treatment will produce tensile elongation above 15% and a significant ductility increase over the as-cast state.
Failure will shift from interfacial cracking to uniform plastic deformation with high strain-hardening rates.
The as-cast alloy has a fracture stress of 944 MPa and an elongation of 25.6%.
The as-cast baseline exhibits brittle failure at phase interfaces.
Processing above about 1300 °C can generate brittle Laves phases and should therefore be avoided in the target alloy.
HIP at 1230 °C can precipitate an HCP secondary phase associated with extreme tensile brittleness.
The successful pressure window must induce severe plastic deformation without causing phase separation or excessive grain growth.
Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni specimens conventionally HIP-treated at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 hours are predicted to retain unrefined lamellae, show brittle fracture, and have less than 5% elongation.

contradictions.description: The initial state is characterized as having low ductility and catastrophic interfacial cracking, whereas the stated baseline elongation is 25.6%, which is substantial and is not accompanied by cited evidence of catastrophic interfacial failure.

An elongation target of greater than 15% is described as a significant increase over an as-cast baseline reported to have 25.6% elongation; merely exceeding 15% would not demonstrate an increase over that baseline.
